fixture_name: Cloverleaf-to-urban interchange conversion — INT preliminary design (Wikimedia PD geometry)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: A shortened collector-distributor weave at 1,100 pcu/h with concentrated lane-change demand is a substantive sideswipe/rear-end safety concern.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-IN-015 supplies a verbatim prompt on junction suitability, channelling, lane balance, and through-lane continuity, and EV-IN-004 supports the PIARC checklist context.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: The finding remains a safety concern at preliminary design and uses PIARC prompts without conflating compliance questions with safety issues.
justifications.recommendation_quality: It proposes concrete verification steps and specific mitigation options: lengthening the weave or adding ramp metering if inadequacy is confirmed.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are acknowledged as not exposed because shared-use paths are grade-separated, so the not-applicable case is explicitly handled.

justifications.substance: Uncontrolled ramp-terminal crossings for shared-use path users create a substantive VRU safety gap against stated scheme objectives.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Both cited evidence items include verbatim quotes supporting pedestrian/cyclist provision and all-road-user consideration at junctions.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: The finding stays a PIARC preliminary-design safety concern and does not misstate a compliance requirement.
justifications.recommendation_quality: The recommendation specifies controlled or grade-separated crossings and signalisation at identified ramp-terminal interfaces.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly identified and their uncontrolled crossing exposure is central to the finding.
